picks.title: Five Candidates For Yukta-Vairagya
picks.summary: “Rupa Gosvami says that as long as we are in this material world we have to act; we cannot cease acting. Therefore if actions are performed and the fruits are given to Krishna, then that is called yukta-vairagya. Actually situated in renunciation, such activities clear the mirror of the mind, and as the actor gradually makes progress in spiritual realization he becomes completely surrendered to the Supreme Personality of Godhead.” (Shrila Prabhupada, Bhagavad-gita, 9.28 Purport)
picks.reason: Explores acting with renunciation and surrender to Krishna per Bhagavad-gita teachings.

picks.title: Put Up a Sign
picks.summary: “Engage your mind always in thinking of Me, offer obeisances and worship Me. Being completely absorbed in Me, surely you will come to Me.” (Lord Krishna, Bhagavad-gita, 9.34)
picks.reason: Focuses on devotion and absorption in Krishna from the Bhagavad-gita.

picks.title: 1825: Our Labels Are Warping Our Vision | The Many Ways We Respond to Krishna
picks.summary: I'm a man. I'm a woman. I'm American. I'm this, I'm that. Every label we carry colors how we see the world, ourselves and God. Yoga starts from a bold premise: our perception is clouded, and it can be cleared. Bhakti goes further still. As the lens clears, a love unique to each of us awakens. Raghunath and Kaustubha explore that teaching through Krishna's entrance into Kamsa's wrestling arena, where the same boy stirs terror in one heart, wonder in another, and varieties of love in others. Srimad Bhagavatam 10.42.32 - 10.43.40 Nārada Pañcarātra, quoted in Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya 19.170  **
picks.reason: Explores perception, labels, and unique love for Krishna through bhakti yoga.
